newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle called steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle called steady to lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures were both expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Spot June live cattle could hold steady on support from lack of delivery notices. The fact that cash cattle was trading at $63 per cwt instead of $62 as some traders had feared was also supportive, analysts said.

However, deferred months were expected to remain under technical pressure after tumbling for losses late Monday. Expectations Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report will show rising fed cattle supllies should also weigh on prices, they said.

Early analyst projections put total onfeed cattle supplies in the major 7-state area between 112 and 114 percent of a year ago as of June 1. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates ranged from 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings 97 to 100 percent.
Feeder cattle futures were also expected to show carryover pressure following the lower CME feeder cattle index and steady to higher corn futures indication.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.18 at $77.58 per cwt. However, the index is still hovering around its highest level since mid August, 1994.
